- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce forecast slope to avoid overshoot.
- If recent history shows a sharp peak followed by rapid decline, model should not overcorrect downward — expect mean reversion in 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is flat or rising, reduce forecast slightly to avoid overconfidence in recovery.
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome by 5–10% over 30-day horizon, apply downward bias correction — especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- For spikes in history (e.g., 90+), model should not assume continuation — expect mean reversion or reversal within 7–10 days unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–0.3) and forecast is smooth, introduce slight volatility in forecast to reflect sentiment uncertainty.
- When true outcome drops sharply after a forecast peak, reduce forecast by 5–15% for next period to account for sentiment-driven correction.
